blocks.x: What had happened -- the reason that this woman knew me, was because I had done a lot of transcriptions for the BBC. And actually, I supposed, I was getting heard in Great Britain before I was heard here in the United States.
How were those made?
There were made in the studio in large transcriptions, and then they mailed them over there and played them on the BBC.
In fact, I guess all those early things

that I did were sent over there, because in 1938 every thing had happened. You know, 'Loch Lomond' (inaudible) and I was known all over because 'Loch Lomond' hit the world.
So then most of these earlier things -- these little (inaud) Italian records, I supposed they might've been released over there before they were released over here. you look,
I think when most of them are also issued in Great Britain.
Sure. Well anyway --
On Parlophone --

In '38, I was supposed to -- you know, they were negotiating for me to go to Great Britain, and especially to go to Scotland. But, you know, the war was imminent so I didn't get to go. I really didn't get over there until ten years later, 1948.
And I discovered that the 'Folks Who Lived On The Hill' had been on the 'Housewife's Parade' for ten years -- playing it everyday.
I guess -- everything I did I guess was

released over there as soon as, or mabye before it was released here in the United States.
These transcriptions for the BBC, this is a separate thing to your --
Yeah. These were not recordings per se. They were actually transcriptions made for broadcasting purposes.
Same musicians --
Yes.

Oh yes. No. Well yes. Those early arecordings were made with the same guys. That was another gig, you know.
